title: Teodora Ana Mihai On Her Breakout Feature ‘Heysel 85’ & Plans For Her Next Film — Tokyo
full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News Daytime Emmy Winners: ‘General Hospital’ Wins Sixth Best Drama Series In A Row; ‘Kelly Clarkson’ Takes Talk Series Trophy In Final Year Read the full story By Zac Ntim Zac Ntim International Reporter @ZacharyNtim More Stories By Zac Cate Blanchett, Shahrbanoo Sadat & Mohammad Rasoulof Bring Displacement Film Fund To Tokyo With Help From ‘Perfect Days’ Actor Kōji Yakusho Camerimage: Hype Williams & Darren Aronofsky Set For Honorary Awards Toho CEO Matsuoka Hiro On The Company’s Decision To Self-Distribute ‘Godzilla Minus One’ In The U.S. — Tokyo View All October 30, 2026 10:31pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source 'Heysel 85' Courtesy of Menuetto Film After a buzzy debut almost eight months ago in Berlin, Teodora Ana Mihai has finally begun the international launch of her latest feature, Heysel 85 , and this week the Romanian-Belgian filmmaker is at the Tokyo Film Festival, where the film has received its Asian premiere. Directed by Mihai, from a screenplay she co-wrote with Lode Desmet and Isabelle Darras, Heysel 85 is inspired by the 1985 Heysel Stadium disaster in Brussels, where 39 people died ahead of the European Cup Final between Liverpool and Juventus. “This is one of those moments in Belgium that’s comparable to 9/11 in the US. It was a huge event; people were shocked,” Mihai says of the disaster’s legacy in Belgium. Related Stories News Japan's Animation Industry Grows 15.8% To Record $28BN, Driven By Both Domestic & Overseas Sales - TIFFCOM News Cate Blanchett, Shahrbanoo Sadat & Mohammad Rasoulof Bring Displacement Film Fund To Tokyo With Help From 'Perfect Days' Actor Kōji Yakusho “Belgium is divided in many ways. We have different language-speaking communities. But everyone is united on this: What happened there should not have happened. The shock is shared, and it still lives on today.” Watch on Deadline Mihai’s story follows Marie, the mayor’s daughter (Violet Braeckman), and a journalist of Italian origin (Matteo Simoni) covering the match for Italian TV, accompanied by family. Before kick-off, hooligans go on the rampage. Dozens of people die; chaos ensues. While continuing to report, Luca searches for his family. And Marie has to step in for her father, who, drunk and overwhelmed, is no longer capable of taking command. The politicians and police are faced with the question: cancel the match or let it go on? Mihai says she only considered tackling the Heysel story after her producer, Hans Everaert, suggested she take a look at some material on the disaster. “I didn’t jump at it right away,” Mihai says. “I wondered, ‘Am I the right person to tell this story?’ There were so many reasons why I shouldn’t. But perhaps because it was outside my comfort zone, I should do it. Maybe I could make something of it that people wouldn’t expect—and that’s not always a bad thing.” Mihai adds that she was particularly interested in football’s “metaphorical potential,” which made it the “perfect backdrop for saying something existential.” Mihai’s intentions are clear throughout. Heysel 85 doesn’t spend much time recreating the deadly events; the picture instead focuses on interrogating the structural flaws that allowed it to happen. The film is constructed using a mix of archival footage from the disaster and live action sequences that Mihai shot on vibrant 16mm on the advice of her DoP Marius Panduru, whom she describes as “one of the best cinematographers in Romania.” “He told me from the very beginning, ‘If you want the archive to look as close as possible to what we’re going to film, 16mm is the way to go. Forget about filters; you can get close, but it’s never going to be the same.,’” Mihai says of Panduru’s advice. “This is our third film, and we’re preparing our fourth. I like to keep my collaborators close if the collaboration goes well.” 16mm celluloid film meant Mihai had to slash days off her production schedule to cut costs. “We didn’t have a lot of time; a lot of it was quite impulsive, but the right attitude and energy were there,” she says. “I really believe the production looks better than the money we had available. Everyone was committed.” Mihai’s two previous feature titles are Waiting for August (2014) and Traffic (2024). Heysel 85 opens in Belgium on November 18 via Kinepolis, and in the UK on November 20 through Icon . “There’s been a lot of positive buzz, but you can never know until it’s out there,” she says of the upcoming release. “We premiered in Berlin, and then we had to wait. The distributor decided to release it at this time of year because it’s better for films in general. In the summer, we want to make the most of the little bit of sun we have in Belgium, rather than sit in the cinema, so I’m very curious.” In the meantime, Mihai says she is already back at work, working on her fourth feature, currently titled Two Lives , which she describes as a chamber piece about two brothers and their respective families. “It starts as a happy summer holiday that they repeat every year. Then tragedy strikes, and one of the brothers dies,” Mihai says. “The film becomes about his widow and how she crumbles from all sides but still has to function because she has two teenage boys. The film looks at this woman, whom everyone expects to keep functioning, because there’s no pause button on motherhood.” Mihai adds: “It’s a very uncomfortable project. I love it. Hopefully it will make people think. I’ve always loved the mirrors that cinema and art hold up to us, and I hope this will be one of them.” The Tokyo Film Festival runs until Nov 4. ‘Beyond The Gates’ Scores Big In First Year; Red Carpet Photo Gallery Hello Sunshine Cuts Half Of Staff After Acquisition By Witherspoon & Mediawan ‘Clayface’ & ‘You Can See Everything’ Brawling For Halloween Weekend Crown Classic Horror Pics & TV Episodes, Scary Triple Bills, Final Girls, Monsters, More Read More About: Comments

title: How Keanu Reeves Landed in Stop-Motion Samurai Epic ‘Hidari’ – and Why S.S. Rajamouli Wanted to Know How It Was Made
full_text: × Oct 30, 2026 9:38pm PT How Keanu Reeves Landed in Stop-Motion Samurai Epic ‘Hidari’ – and Why S.S. Rajamouli Wanted to Know How It Was Made By Naman Ramachandran Plus Icon Naman Ramachandran Latest Sanjay Gupta, Indian Director of ‘Kaante’ and ‘Zinda,’ Dies at 59 5 hours ago Sourav Ganguly’s ‘Bigg Boss Bangla’ Among Highlights as Indian Media Giant JioStar Revenues Climb 10% 9 hours ago How Keanu Reeves Landed in Stop-Motion Samurai Epic ‘Hidari’ – and Why S.S. Rajamouli Wanted to Know How It Was Made 10 hours ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Courtesy of Hidari Inc. Keanu Reeves joined Japanese stop-motion feature “ Hidari ” after watching the project’s pilot film, with his team getting back to the filmmakers about a week after the screening was arranged to set up a Zoom call, director Kawamura Masashi said at the Tokyo International Film Festival , where he also updated the film’s fundraising push. Kawamura, who created, wrote and is directing “Hidari,” appeared with co-director Ogawa Iku at a session reporting on Film Frontier, a talent development program backed by Japan’s Agency for Cultural Affairs and run by festival organizer UniJapan. The program has paid for the team’s travel to markets and industry events. Related Stories ‘God of War’s’ Bruno Velazquez, ‘Mandalorian & Grogu’s’ Hal Hickel Detail Cinema-Gaming Crossover at View Conference Reeves’ casting as the lead voice was announced at Cannes in May, but Kawamura said the actor had seen the pilot before the festival. “We were heavily influenced by Kurosawa’s films, so when the puppet was being made, I asked for Mifune Toshiro and Keanu Reeves added together, divided by two and then aged,” Kawamura said. From then on, Kawamura kept Reeves at the top of his list for the lead voice. The film’s producers took that seriously, found a way to reach the actor and arranged for him to watch the pilot. “About a week later we heard back, and it was, ‘OK, let’s do a Zoom,’” Kawamura said. “I was thinking, so this is how fast things move these days. Then we got on the call and Keanu was there on the other side.” “Hidari” has also caught the eye of “RRR” director S.S. Rajamouli . Kawamura said he met the Indian filmmaker at Annecy, showed him “Hidari” and ended up in a standing conversation of about 30 minutes about how the film was made. “He said, ‘You’re amazing. How did you make this?’” Kawamura said. Kawamura said an encounter like that, with a director he would rarely cross paths with otherwise, could only happen at a festival. “There’s the surprise inside the theater, and there are the connections after you walk out,” he said. The team shot the proof-of-concept short around three years ago, paying for it themselves with help from crowdfunding, and posted it on YouTube. It has since drawn about 5.3 million views and roughly 120,000 followers, many of them overseas, according to Kawamura. “Wood carving, stop-motion and a period drama – it’s a very austere project,” he said. “If we’d pitched it with just a written proposal, I don’t think anyone would have understood it.” With Film Frontier support, the filmmakers pitched “Hidari” at the Annecy Animation Showcase, part of the Cannes Film Market, carrying one of the hand-carved puppets with them. Kawamura said the puppet drew bigger crowds than its makers, and the Cannes platform put the film in front of live-action and action fans as well as distributors and agents. “Stop-motion is a really small world, and people tend to assume it’s a narrow market,” Kawamura said. “But even though it’s stop-motion, we think of it as an action film.” The budget is large, and the team is still out selling the project, seeking grants and partnerships with overseas distributors, Kawamura said. “In terms of speed, we’re making it the indie way,” he added. “Thanks to being light on our feet, I think the project has managed to make it across thin ice.” Earlier this month in Busan, Dwarf Studios producer Matsumoto Noriko said talks with a U.S. company that had offered to fund the entire budget, in exchange for all the rights, had stalled. Ogawa, who works at stop-motion house Dwarf Studios, attended Annecy this year. He said the technique remains niche in commercial film and TV animation, but festival shorts and student sections are full of it, and studios from Europe, North America and beyond converge on Annecy. “When I took the puppet along, it was hugely popular,” he said. “It was fun.” Film Frontier, now in its third year, is part of the Agency for Cultural Affairs’ Creator Support Fund, which backs creators for around three years, from project development through to overseas rollout. title: Georgia’s ‘Guria’ Wins Best Film at Asia Pacific Screen Awards as Thailand’s Sompot Chidgasornpongse Takes Director Prize
full_text: × Oct 30, 2026 9:25pm PT Georgia’s ‘Guria’ Wins Best Film at Asia Pacific Screen Awards as Thailand’s Sompot Chidgasornpongse Takes Director Prize By Naman Ramachandran Plus Icon Naman Ramachandran Latest Sanjay Gupta, Indian Director of ‘Kaante’ and ‘Zinda,’ Dies at 59 5 hours ago Sourav Ganguly’s ‘Bigg Boss Bangla’ Among Highlights as Indian Media Giant JioStar Revenues Climb 10% 9 hours ago How Keanu Reeves Landed in Stop-Motion Samurai Epic ‘Hidari’ – and Why S.S. Rajamouli Wanted to Know How It Was Made 10 hours ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Asia Pacific Screen Awards Georgian filmmaker Levan Koguashvili’s “Guria” was named best film at the 19th Asia Pacific Screen Awards , handed out Oct. 30 at The Star Gold Coast in Queensland, Australia. Koguashvili shared the prize with fellow producers Olena Yershova and Boris Frumin. The film was made across seven countries: Georgia, Switzerland, Luxembourg, Bulgaria, Türkiye, Norway and Saudi Arabia. Related Stories ‘God of War’s’ Bruno Velazquez, ‘Mandalorian & Grogu’s’ Hal Hickel Detail Cinema-Gaming Crossover at View Conference Thai director Sompot Chidgasornpongse won best director for “9 Temples to Heaven,” a co-production involving Thailand, Singapore, France, Norway, China, Hong Kong, Indonesia and Qatar. Myanmar’s Aung Phyoe received a special mention in the directing category for “Fruit Gathering.” Afghan director Shahrbanoo Sadat took the Jury Grand Prize for “No Good Men.” This year’s field comprised 36 nominated films from 32 countries and regions. Nepalese actor Pushpa Thing Lama won best performance for “Elephants in the Fog,” and South Korea’s Sim Su-bin was named best new performer for “The World Before.” The screenplay award went to Rakan Mayasi, Wahid Ajmi and Pôl Seif for “Yesterday the Eye Didn’t Sleep,” backed by Belgium, Lebanon, Palestine, Qatar and Saudi Arabia. Vietnamese cinematographer Nguyễn Vinh Phúc won for “Hearing.” New Zealand’s Paloma Schneideman took best youth film for “Big Girls Don’t Cry,” produced by Vicky Pope and Thomas Coppell. The animation prize went to “The Violinist,” a co-production between Singapore, Spain and Italy that was co-directed by Singapore’s Ervin Han and Spain’s Raúl García. Itab Azzam and Jack MacInness won best documentary for “One in a Million,” a U.K.-U.S. film that follows the life of a Syrian refugee. Isabelle Kalandar, who both directed and produced “Another Birth,” received the Cultural Diversity Award for the Tajikistan, U.S. and Qatar collaboration. India’s R. Gowtham earned the Young Cinema Award, given with NETPAC, for “Members of the Problematic Family.” Malaysian filmmaker Haziqah Azemi won the Forum Filmmaker Award, run with The Post Lounge Group, for her project “Garek.” The story centers on a woman whose relationship is tested when she faces religious persecution after becoming pregnant outside marriage. Azemi, who took part in the Griffith Film School and APSA Regional Reels program, came back to APSA this year after developing the project with mentoring from APSA Academy member Yulia Evina Bhara. Tracey Vieira, chair of the Asia Pacific Screen Awards, said: “From ‘Guria’ and ‘No Good Men’ to ‘Elephants in the Fog,’ this year’s winners remind us of the extraordinary stories emerging from our region and the importance of creating opportunities for these voices to be recognized internationally.” Veteran Indian producer Bobby Bedi was handed the FIAPF Award for outstanding contribution to film in the Asia Pacific. Luis Alberto Scalella, president of FIAPF, said: “Through landmark films such as ‘Bandit Queen’ and ‘Fire,’ he has championed powerful stories that have challenged audiences and resonated far beyond India.” The ceremony also revealed five projects selected for the 2026 MPA APSA Academy Film Fund, each of which will get a $10,000 grant funded entirely by the Motion Picture Association. They are Payal Kapadia’s “A Memory of Being Here” (India), produced by Thomas Hakim; Davy Chou’s “My Father’s Glory” (France, Cambodia), produced by Charlotte Vincent; Taifeng Liu’s “A Place in the Sun” (China), produced by Janet (Yan Yan) Wu; Nicole Midori Woodford’s “Incarnation” (Singapore, Japan), produced by Anthony Chen; and Zhanana Kurmasheva’s documentary “The Story of My Shirt” (Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, Kyrgyzstan, China, Chile), produced by Banu Ramazanova. Three of the five projects are directed by women. Chen returns to the fund after working on “We Are All Strangers,” which received a grant in 2023 and was among this year’s nominees. Urmila Venugopalan, president and managing director, Asia Pacific, at the Motion Picture Association, said the success of films such as “9 Temples to Heaven,” which received MPA APSA Academy Film Fund support in 2021, “shows the importance of supporting filmmakers and their stories from the earliest stages of development.” Every APSA nominee, along with members of the nominations councils and juries, joins the APSA Academy, whose president is Australian screen veteran Jack Thompson. The body now has upward of 1,816 members across 84 countries and areas. The full list of winners: Best Film “Guria,” dir. Levan Koguashvili; prod. Olena Yershova, Levan Koguashvili, Boris Frumin (Georgia, Switzerland, Luxembourg, Bulgaria, Türkiye, Norway, Saudi Arabia) Jury Grand Prize Shahrbanoo Sadat, “No Good Men” (Germany, France, Norway, Denmark, Afghanistan) Best Director Sompot Chidgasornpongse, “9 Temples to Heaven” (Thailand, Singapore, France, Norway, China, Hong Kong, Indonesia, Qatar) Best Director – Special Mention Aung Phyoe, “Fruit Gathering” (Myanmar, Czech Republic, France) Best Youth Film “Big Girls Don’t Cry,” dir. title: Angel Studios CCO Lays Out “Values-Based” Initiative Banning Sex, Nudity, F-Words & “Misuse Of God’s Name”: “Hollywood Lives In A Bubble”
full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News Daytime Emmy Winners: ‘General Hospital’ Wins Sixth Best Drama Series In A Row; ‘Kelly Clarkson’ Takes Talk Series Trophy In Final Year Read the full story By Glenn Garner Glenn Garner Associate Editor @xoxo_glenn More Stories By Glenn Angel Studios CCO Lays Out “Values-Based” Initiative Banning Sex, Nudity, F-Words & “Misuse Of God’s Name”: “Hollywood Lives In A Bubble” ‘Real Time’: Bill Maher Reacts To Trump’s “Longest Ever” 1,300+ Word Tweet Berating Him: “Kind Of A Flex” Selma Blair Breaks Silence On JFK Airport Arrest: “I Take This Very Seriously” View All October 30, 2026 8:16pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Angel Studios Angel Studios Five years into Angel Studios ‘ launch, the Christian production company and distributor is implementing “The Angel Promise” content standards. Co-founder and CCO Jeff Harmon explained that the initiative bans on-screen sex, nudity, the F-word and “misuse of God’s name,” in addition to expanding parental controls and allowing paid subscribers to choose which films and television shows make it to the platform. “I think Hollywood generally kind of lives in a bubble,” Harmon told Fox News . “These are excellent craftsmen. They’re the best storytellers in the world. Hollywood has built the best storytelling infrastructure in the world. Related Stories News Angel Studios’ Membership Guild Hits 3 Million Mark, Doubling Its Year-Ago Level News Kelsey Grammer Meets With Donald Trump In Oval Office During D.C. Visit For ‘Young Washington’ Screening “But at the same time, they’ve kind of drifted more and more away from the values-based audience that they used to serve. And with that, in our view, as brothers and as fathers, as a father, Hollywood hasn’t been giving me consistently what I need. Once in a while, you get a good one, but you have to sift through all these things to find your good movies and your good stories,” he added. Watch on Deadline Harmon noted that Angel Studios is also letting “the audience have a veto right” through the Angel Guild, the platform’s purported 3 million-strong membership. “Our goal was to set out and try to fix this problem of kind of stepping out of the Hollywood bubble and stepping into middle America’s shoes,” added Harmon. title: 2026 Daytime Emmy Awards: ‘General Hospital’ Wins Best Daytime Drama
full_text: × Skip to main content By Hilary Lewis Plus Icon Hilary Lewis Deputy Editor, East Coast hilarylewis Follow Sign Up View All October 30, 2026 8:11pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Daytime Emmy nominee Amanda Setton, with Troy Lennon Appel, in 'General Hospital.' Disney/Christine Bartolucci The 2026 Daytime Emmy Awards were presented Friday night, with General Hospital taking home the top prize of best daytime drama. The series, which went into Friday night’s show up for 13 awards, won three other awards and saw its Genie Francis receive the lifetime achievement award. Beyond the Gates also won four awards, with star Tamara Tunie winning best actress in a daytime drama series. Best actor in a daytime drama went to The Bold and the Beautiful ‘s Scott Clifton. Tunie, who won her first Daytime Emmy, paid tribute to the “host of Black actresses who paved the way for me, and I feel them as I stand here tonight, beginning with the legendary Cicely Tyson, the first Black woman to appear on a daytime television show, The Guiding Light .” Related Stories TV The Hollywood Reporter Wins 2026 Daytime Emmy Award Music Tom Morello, Annie Lennox, 'KPop Demon Hunters' Songwriters Honored at 2026 SONA Awards Fellow best actress nominee Heather Tom, from The Bold and the Beautiful , was eyeing a record-setting seventh trophy, which would have made her the most awarded actress in daytime history. The Young and the Restless led this year’s nominees with 18 nominations. Though it only won three awards, two of those came in the supporting performer categories. Roger Howarth was named best supporting actor, and Beth Maitland was named best supporting actress. The Kelly Clarkson Show won five awards, including best daytime talk series, but the singer-host of the now-completed talk show didn’t appear to be at the Daytime Emmys . And Clarkson didn’t win the award for best daytime talk series host. Instead that honor went to fellow former talk show host Sherri Shepherd, whose eponymous talk show was canceled after four seasons. Other notable winners include Tracee Ellis Ross, who won best travel and adventure program for her Solo Traveling show; Keke Palmer, who won for her work executive producing Glam Through the Ages ; and Ina Garten, who won best culinary host for her Be My Guest Food Network series, which was named best culinary instructional series. Midway through the ceremony, NATAS chair Terry O’Reilly offered a timely, political speech, just days ahead of the 2026 midterm elections. Speaking about a congressman who was jailed in 1798 after criticizing the president in print, O’Reilly highlighed the power of the people. “The free press in 1800 was not saved by a court. It was saved by citizens who were engaged and informed,” he said. Turning to the present day, O’Reilly called out “the most sustained effort to control what Americans see and hear in this country that were faced in my lifetime.” He cited specifically journalists being banned from covering the Pentagon and president, the DOJ antitrust investigation into the White House TV press pool and the challenge to the news exemption enjoyed by late night and daytime programs, including The View . “It is not much of a leap, from silencing political speech, to suppressing creative expression,” O’Reilly added. “The characters, the storylines, the points of view that someone in power decides are no longer welcome. Here, in the cradle of Hollywood, this town of all towns, we know where that can lead. We have seen what happens when those in power begin drawing up lists of people and pops and ideas that they are willing to label as un-American. We should never wish to see that again.” Turning to the “consequential” midterms on Tuesday, O’Reilly issued a call to those in the audience: “Let’s stand together to resist those who would seek comfort in a quieter media.” And NATAS additionally inducted a number of individuals into its Gold and Silver Circle Society, recognizing industry leaders who’ve demonstrated enduring contributions to television through their 50 or 25 years in industry. The 2026 Gold Circle inductees are Allen Media Group CEO Byron Allen, performer Patrika Darbo, actor-director-producer Francesca James and host-producer Meredith Vieira. The Silver Circle inductees are Fox TV Stations executive vp, programming and development Stephen Brown and announcer warm-up host Rubin Ervin. The Hollywood Reporter won its first Daytime Emmy , taking home the award for best arts and popular culture program for THR ’s Off Script roundtable series. Fellow PMC brand IndieWire additionally won best editing for a daytime studio program for its craft roundtables, with Trevor Wallace accepting for the brand. The 53rd Daytime Emmy Awards ceremony took place on Friday, Oct. 30 at the Hollywood Palladium. A complete list of the 2026 Daytime Emmy Awards winners follows. title: ‘Beyond The Gates’ Wins Four Daytime Emmys In Its First Year Of Eligibility
full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News Daytime Emmy Winners: ‘General Hospital’ Wins Sixth Best Drama Series In A Row; ‘Kelly Clarkson’ Takes Talk Series Trophy In Final Year Read the full story By Lynette Rice Lynette Rice Senior TV Writer @LynetteRice More Stories By Lynette Reggie McFadden Dies: ‘In Living Color’ Comedian Was 57 Isaiah Washington Reveals His Wife’s 2025 Death In Social Media Post: “It Came As A Huge Shock to Me” ‘SNL’s Weekend Update Tackles Cornell Controversy & Return Of ‘Glee’ View All October 30, 2026 8:05pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source 'Beyond the Gates' CBS CBS ‘ Beyond the Gates triumphed at the 53rd annual Daytime Emmy Awards in its first year of eligibility, with big wins in the Outstanding Lead Actor and Emerging Actress categories Friday. In all, Beyond the Gates won four Emmys at the ceremony that was streamed on YouTube. The sudser penned by Michele Val Jean debuted on CBS on February 24, 2025, which meant it missed the cutoff window for the 2025 awards. Related Stories News Daytime Emmys: ‘General Hospital’ Wins Sixth Best Drama Series In A Row; ‘Kelly Clarkson Show’ Wins In Final Year – Full Winners List News Daytime Emmy Awards 2026 Photos: Best Of The Red Carpet But Gates , which is set in one of the most affluent Black counties in the United States, made up for lost time Friday as stars Tamara Tunie and Ambyr Michelle received first-time Daytime Emmys for their roles as Anita Dupree and Eva Thomas, respectively. “This is the best welcome back to daytime ever,” said Tunie after accepting the Emmy. (She’s an alum of As the World Turns and Days of Our Lives ). “There are a host of Black actresses who paved the way for me and I feel them as I stand here tonight, beginning with Cicely Tyson, the first Black woman to appear on the daytime TV show The Guiding Light.” Watch on Deadline The CBS sudser also won Emmys for lighting direction and hairstyling and makeup. It earned 13 nominations in its first year of eligibility. Beyond the Gates , the first daytime soap opera to feature a primarily Black cast since Generations in 1989, has been renewed through the 2027-28 season. title: Bill Maher Responds to Trump’s 1,318-Word Social Rant: “He Went Off on Me Like Kelly Clarkson in a Toy Store”
full_text: Skip to main content By McKinley Franklin Plus Icon McKinley Franklin View All October 30, 2026 7:38pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Bill Maher on 'Real Time.' Screenshot Logo text Bill Maher has responded to President Donald Trump ‘s lengthy social media post where he slammed him as a “complete and total loser,” and shared more details about their recent dinner at the White House. During Friday’s episode of Real Time with Bill Maher , the comedian addressed a few of the statements made in Trump’s post. He began the monologue by discussing the upcoming midterms and how former President Barack Obama caused a “big scandal” for a comment he made at a campaign rally saying that Trump has “got the White House looking like Saddam Hussein opened a Cheesecake Factory.” Related Stories Music Canadian Rock Icon Bryan Adams Takes Aim at Trump, Says His Protest Song Gets Standing Ovations in Red States (Exclusive) Music Bryan Adams Releases New Trump Protest Song "Lake Ontario" Maher said, “And the Republicans all said, ‘Leave the Cheesecake Factory out of this!’ Well, I mean, I should know. I just had dinner there. I hear it went well. What have you heard?” The host then asked, “Now, did you see the 1,300-word Tweet he sent out? Longest ever. Kind of a flex.” He joked that “dining at the White House is the opposite of the Cheesecake Factory. After you leave, they review you.” “He went off on me like Kelly Clarkson in a toy store,” Maher added. “I mean, eating with Trump is like dating Taylor Swift. It’s a lot of laughs at the time, but later on, they’re tearing you a new asshole.” Maher was then handed a printed copy of Trump’s Truth Social post, and began to “address a few of the allegations.” Before that, he noted, “Look, I don’t want it to be this way. The whole point of having these dinners was talk, disagree, but listen, which he does in person, but don’t hate each other. And then I go back to my job here and then the heartaches begin.” “It begins, ‘Let’s talk about the complete and total loser Bill Maher.’ You got me there. I’ll own that,” Maher joked, going on to explain “what pisses me off” is that “he doesn’t even notice what I say,” specifically citing a line in Trump’s post where he wrote, “[Maher] doesn’t think it was a good thing to take the Nuclear Weapon away from Iran, which shows you that he is not very smart.” Real Time then played a series of clips showcasing the opposite of Trump’s claim. Maher then moved on to another section: “Page two, he talks about how I call him incessantly. I’ve never called you, you call me. I’d be afraid to call you. You’re the president. I think you’re too busy. Well, plainly not. He’s talking about me, ‘He invited himself to the White House.’ As if you could do that. ‘Sir, Bill Maher is here.’ ‘Well, he’s not invited, but the law.” He also read aloud Trump writing that Maher is a “major POTHEAD.” Maher’s response: “Well, I guess the cat’s out of the bag now. Boy, that explains a lot. I thought I was just happy.” (Later in the Real Time episode, Kid Rock, who was at the dinner, told Maher he was “pretty high” at the White House.) He continued reading Trump’s post, “‘Bill had alcohol in his hand,’ that you gave me, ‘as he walked through the White House,’ and then — I love this — ‘Overall, I thought it was a good meeting.'” “‘I understand he’s doing his thing. I never took it personally,'” Maher recited, dumbfounded. “‘He’s not a nice guy, and what he spouts isn’t what he believes. He has to cater to his base, which is mostly composed of losers,’ that would be you assholes,” the host said to his audience. Trump penned a 1,318-word Truth Social post on Sunday, where he criticized Maher, Real Time and producer Chuck LaBella. He wrote, “Let’s talk about this COMPLETE AND TOTAL LOSER, Bill Maher. He’s got a Low Rated Show on equally Low Rated HBO, which was once, long ago, a Network of Quality and Excitement — But that’s all gone. It’s not ‘HOT’ anymore! Maher’s friend and business associate, Chuck LaBella, was also a friend of mine, worked on The Top Hit Show, The Apprentice, as a ‘gofer’ and, because of the success of that show, Number One and Top Rated on many weeks, with the Finale’ being among the Top Shows of the Year, he was automatically and quickly brought up through the Ranks of NBC, along with everyone else associated with that Historic ‘Happening.'” Trump’s post seemingly was made in response to jokes Maher made during his monologue on the Oct. 23 episode. “It’s just a little odd that Trump keeps gushing about men’s bodies, and how handsome they are, and their jawlines, and their asses, their physiques,” said Maher. “I’m a little hurt. I was there for dinner for four hours last week, and not a peep. Nothing.” Maher said, “Trump has the lowest approval rating of any midterm candidate ever. title: Timbaland Files $15 Million Fraud Lawsuit Against Former Managers
full_text: × Skip to main content By Ethan Millman Plus Icon Ethan Millman Music Editor View All October 30, 2026 6:23pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Timbaland Leon Bennett/Getty Images for The Recording Academy Timbaland has filed a $15 million lawsuit against his former manager and business manager, accusing the two executives of fraud, breach of fiduciary duty and civil theft, among other claims. In a 65-page suit filed in Los Angeles Superior Court on Friday, Timbaland alleges that the manager, Gary Marella, “stole millions in unauthorized commissions, fees, and reimbursements,” used Timbaland’s funds to pay Marella’s employees, and “falsified financial records and communications to conceal unauthorized payments” from the producer. Related Stories Lifestyle Snoop Dogg's 'Doggyland' Expanding Children's Book Series (Exclusive First Look) Movies David Bowie Returns to Berlin With Immersive Event The former business manager Bruce Seckendorf, Timbaland, whose real name is Timothy Mosley, alleges, “failed to pay Mosley’s mortgage and allowed his home to reach the brink of foreclosure.” The suit claims Seckendorf’s firm “failed to timely pay substantial federal taxes, causing millions in penalties and interest, while continuing to pay themselves, the Marella Defendants, and other professionals millions in commissions, fees, and purported loan repayments.” “Defendants used their entrusted authority to enrich themselves and others, conceal financial misconduct, and deplete Timbaland’s valuable assets,” the suit says. “Plaintiffs seek to recover their losses, compel an accounting, and stop the continuing unauthorized use of Timbaland’s name for Defendants’ benefit.” Per the suit, Timbaland only learned of the alleged misconduct because he got a foreclosure notice at his home last year. After receiving the notice, the suit says, Timbaland called Seckendorf, who the producer says failed to “clearly explain why his office had failed to make the mortgage payments without informing Mosley.” Timbaland subsequently took on independent legal counsel and financial representatives, who had investigated the issue, “uncovering unauthorized payments, concealed credit-card arrangements, falsified communications, undisclosed liabilities, and purported loans Mosley had never knowingly agreed to,” the suit states. “The foreclosure was not caused simply because Plaintiffs had no money,” the complaint says, adding that the “Seckendorf Defendants thus prioritized nearly $900,000 in payments to Defendants and attorneys they engaged in five months, while failing to pay for twelve months of mortgage arrears they caused and concealed from Mosley.” Per the suit, the two defendants were terminated in 2025. Seckendorf and his firm didn’t immediately responded to request for comment. In a comment, Marella said that “I strongly dispute these allegations.” “Unfortunately, Tim is attempting to shift responsibility for his own overspending and financial decisions onto someone else (again) as he did before we managed him,” Marella said. “When I began managing him in 2017, long after producing his biggest hits, he was already broke and in debt, had spent all of his money, and was living in a rental. His financial problems did not begin with me. I came in to help rebuild his business. Over approximately nine years, we generated roughly $75 million in business. Despite that, Tim continued spending beyond his means, ultimately having to sell his home last year due to his actions and move into a rental in Coral Gables. Those were the consequences of his own financial decisions, no one else.” Timbaland first started working directly with Marella and Seckendorf in 2016 while dealing with financial misconduct claims against his previous representation, according to the complaint. Marella is the CEO of Mono Music Group, which along with Timbaland has represented other hitmakers such as Poo Bear and ATL Jacob. Seckendorf is a partner at LL Business Management, which was listed on Billboard’s top business managers list last year and represents the likes of Feid, Pusha T, Clipse and Cirkut among others. Mono Music Group, LL Business Management and the firm Seckendorf Hasson Reilly & Kobay CPA’s are all co-defendants in the suit as well. Marella and Seckendorf had worked with Timbaland during a period of significant business ventures for the producer, including launching his popular Verzuz series with Swizz Beatz during the pandemic and selling his catalog to Hipgnosis Songs Fund back in 2019. Regarding Verzuz in particular, Timbaland alleges that Marella took $500,000 more than he was entitled to on two separate incidents relating to $5 million payments from the venture. On the Hipgnosis sale, Marella took $775,000 more than his allotted 10 percent commission would’ve called for, the suit says. Tim was fully aware of the 15 percent commission I received on the Hipgnosis catalog sale,” Marella said. “We spent more than a year and a half helping organize his business affairs and resolve outstanding issues to make that transaction possible. Calling that compensation unauthorized now does not erase his knowledge of the arrangement at the time. I stand behind it and will substantiate through the legal process. As for Verzuz, he was aware of our management commission. His business manager paid us with Tim’s approval.” Marella also co-founded the beat marketplace Beatclub with Timbaland, though as the suit alleges, Marella “grossly mismanaged” the company and treated Mosley as a piggy bank to repair the problems he created. The suit claims Marella “depleted investor funds, spent company money contrary to how he represented it would be used, incurred obligations Beatclub could not pay, failed to pay employees and creators he hired, and spent money contrary to board restrictions.” Marella called Beatclub, “a startup,” further stating that “the ups and downs are par for the course. We launched the platform in 2019, raised outside investment, and together contributed more than $1 million of our own money. In 2024, we let go of most of the staff and had to rebuild. The company’s financial challenges do not, by themselves, establish misconduct by anyone.” Seckendorf, Timbaland alleges, “knowingly provided substantial assistance through payment authorizations, disbursements, and control over Plaintiffs’ financial accounts, thereby substantially enabling the misconduct and contributing to Plaintiffs’ resulting harm.” Timbaland also brings claims for fraudulent concealment, breach of contract and misappropriation of name, photograph and likeness. “Defendants spent much of their careers benefiting from Timbaland’s career, catalog, reputation, and relationships,” the suit says, “yet left Plaintiffs with depleted assets, undisclosed liabilities, costly litigation, and the burden of reconstructing their own financial affairs.” This story was updated at 8:27 p.m. PST to include comment from Gary Marella on the lawsuit. title: The Hollywood Reporter Wins 2026 Daytime Emmy Award

Beau Grealy The Hollywood Reporter ‘s Off Script roundtable series has won its first Daytime Emmy Award. The awards -season showcase was recognized at the 2026 Daytime Emmys Friday night, where it won in the arts and popular culture category after receiving its third consecutive nomination . In total, the series has garnered six Daytime Emmy nominations since 2017. Off Script beat out fellow nominees Beyond the Gates: Welcome to the Neighborhood: An Entertainment Tonight Special (CBS Media Ventures), Variety & CNN Actors on Actors (CNN Digital | Variety), Variety Studio: Actors on Actors (PBS) and Working in the Theatre (AmericanTheatreWing.org). The series consists of five episodes of Emmy contenders: drama actress, drama actor, comedy actress, comedy actor and stand-up. Executive producer Elisabeth D. Rabishaw accepted the award for THR . Rabishaw thanked the National Academy of Television Arts and Sciences “for the recognition” and praised the fellow nominees in the category. Among those thanked, Rabishaw singled out former AMC Networks exec Blake Callaway, who she noted greenlit the series, and thanked all of those at AMC Networks who worked on the show. Talent on last year’s roster included Seth Rogen, Parker Posey, Helen Mirren, Keri Russell, Kristen Bell, Michelle Williams, Ted Danson, Walton Goggins, Jamie Foxx, Adam Scott, Seth Meyers, Niecy Nash-Betts, Diego Luna and many others. Moderated by THR ’s Lacey Rose and Mikey O’Connell, the series is known for its sharp, unfiltered roundtable format, delivering honest, insightful and often hilarious conversations about the craft and chaos of working in television. But what truly sets Off Script apart is its unmatched ability to curate a who’s who of Hollywood who rarely, if ever, share the same stage. But the roundtable series is not just limited to Emmys season: for the Oscar season roundtables , categories covered include director, actor, actress, songwriter and producer. Postproduction was done by Framework LA. THR has received six Daytime Emmy nominations prior to this, four for the roundtable series. In 2024 and 2025 , THR earned a nom in the same category. In 2024, the publication also earned a nomination for best shortform program with Hollywood Atelier: Rob Pickens , produced by Rovou. Off Script , previously titled Close Up With The Hollywood Reporter , was nominated for three Daytime Emmys in 2021 , 2019 and 2017 . THR also previously won a Los Angeles area Emmy for its roundtable discussion The Hollywood Reporter in Focus: The Wolf of Wall Street , which aired on PBS SoCal. The Daytime Emmy win follows on the heels of THR ’s big showing with the National Arts & Entertainment Journalism Awards earlier this week, where THR received 96 nominations, more than any other outlet. In 2025, THR earned 13 first-place wins at the National Arts & Entertainment Journalism Awards. title: ‘Fuxi: Four Tales of Feasting’ Review: Whimsical Chinese Film Explores Myth and History Through a Series of Tasty Treats
full_text: × Skip to main content By Leslie Felperin Plus Icon Leslie Felperin Contributing Film Critic lesliefelperin Follow Sign Up View All October 30, 2026 5:36pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Fuxi Four Tales of Feasting Uluka Studio Limited Following up his well-received 2021 feature A New Old Play , Sichuan-reared Chinese writer-director Qiu Jiongjiong continues to deploy heightened artifice and quasi-theatrical mannerisms (painted stage sets, rippling cloths representing water, actors in wacky costumes playing astral bodies or dogs, and so on) with his eccentric but addictive latest, Fuxi: Four Tales of Feasting . Although Fuxi runs a trim 135 minutes compared to New Old Play ’s three-hour run time, Qiu still manages to cover more than 2,000 years of myth, history and mythic history with a quartet of stories that revolve around special meals and banquets. (The word “fuxi,” intertitles helpfully explain, can either be a noun meaning delicious food or a verb signifying the savoring of such delicacies.) Related Stories Movies Eric Bauza Remembered as a "Once-in-a-Generation" Talent Who Gave Looney Tunes a New Voice Music Canadian Rock Icon Bryan Adams Takes Aim at Trump, Says His Protest Song Gets Standing Ovations in Red States (Exclusive) Fuxi: Four Tales of Feasting The Bottom Line Spicy and addictive, if not easily digestible. Venue: Tokyo Film Festival (Competition) Cast: Lee Kang Sheng, Lee Hong-Chi, Annie Chen, Fan Guang Yao, Wang Talu, Wang Yitong, Xue Xuchun, Wang Hai, Zhou Jiarui Director/screenwriter: Qiu Jiongjiong 2 hours 15 minutes The different segments, each one offering varying mixtures of slapstick comedy and memento mori solemnity, don’t have much to do with one another story-wise. So Qiu pulls it all together with a framing device about a film crew making each segment, the tales linked by the presence of the sun or Sol (Wen Ke) and Luna aka the moon (Xiao Luxi’); both actors rock massive sun- and moon-shaped headpieces. Yes, the whole thing is just as bizarre as it sounds, but Qiu’s relentless visual brio keeps the soufflé aloft while the serious intent adds a complex, umami aftertaste with a hint of the tingly, numbing flavor so distinctive in Sichuan cuisine. Indeed, much of the dialogue here is reportedly in the Sichuan dialect, a nuance that native speakers are likely to appreciate more than the international viewers, who may have caught this at the Tokyo Film Festival, where it premiered in competition. Nevertheless, the performances and the English-language subtitles succeed in getting across the mix of high and low cultures on display here, as each chapter throws together peasants and aristocrats, ordinary folk and fantastic beings, actors and filmmakers in a giddy muddle. The effect is a little reminiscent of commedia dell’arte with all that breaking-of-the-fourth-wall stuff, especially since the mise en scene here is so archly theatrical. The first minutes kick off with a bit of slightly baffling comic business featuring Sol and Luna interacting with the film crew making the movie we’re presumably watching — although the names of the people playing the roles of “prop master” and “costume designer” and so forth don’t match the names of the real people who actually performed those roles for Fuxi listed in the end credits. Anyway, we soon settle into the first chapter, which takes place “long ago,” when our ancestors, simian-sort of hominids, lived in the forest and had long tails which they believed were “sacred fuxi to be offered at life’s most solemn moments.” And by offered we mean eaten, as is the case with the tail of one aged granny played by veteran Taiwanese actor Lee Kang-Sheng, a frequent collaborator with auteur Tsai Ming-liang. As granny lays dying, her tail is cut off, butchered into chunks like oxtail, stewed and served up to the community, a dish that looks pretty tasty if you don’t mind the self cannibalism. Next comes the second chapter, set in a period of early agrarianism, wherein King Wang, Sichuan’s fourth king, has abdicated the throne and turned into a cuckoo but still flies home to enjoy some tasty fuxi prepared for him annually. Something gets lost in translation here, but the visuals are still rather splendid and props are due to Fan Guang Yao in the role of Wang for the solemnity he manages to muster while wearing giant fake wings and a massive wig of white hair. Ultimately, the third and fourth chapters have the most heft dramatically, making the earlier proceedings feel like pleasant forgettable amuses bouche . The third chapter, set in China’s medieval period, features a quartet of fantastical creatures gathering to remember the life of poet and gastronome Su Dongpo (Lee Hong-Chi), a man of many talents but whose honesty frequently got him into trouble with the powers that be, resulting in several periods of exile. Su’s book boy (Wang Yitong) prepares dishes invented or closely associated with his master for a dinner party consisting of a Harvester (Xue Xuchun) who ferries souls to the underworld, water spirit Yaksha (Wang Hai), an older woman called Granny Spring Dream (Zha Xinji), and a fox in human form (Wang Talu). All enjoy the feast as scenes from Su Dongpo’s life are performed. The final tale revolves around servant boy Zhang Sanxing (Zhou Jiarui), who is living in the early 20th century and witnessing the fall of the Qing dynasty, the last to reign before the ascent of Communism. Once again, Harvester, Yaksha and Fox nosh on fuxi with young Zheng, who is transitioning to the land of the dead, the whole spectacle overseen once again by Sol and Luna before a final pullback to reveal the cast and crew celebrating with food and drink at the wrap party. While it all may not make a huge amount of sense on a first viewing, there is an undoubtable sensual pleasure to be had from Qiu’s painterly sets, the goofy costumes, and the food styling itself. Viewers are advised to watch with an open mind and a full stomach. title: Selma Blair Apologizes for Plane Arrest: “Not One Day Have I Intended to Hurt or Frighten Anyone”
full_text: × Skip to main content By McKinley Franklin Plus Icon McKinley Franklin View All October 30, 2026 5:26pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Selma Blair at the Fashion Trust U.S 2026 Awards at Nya Studios on April 8 in Los Angeles. Charley Gallay/Getty Images Selma Blair is apologizing for her Oct. 11 plane arrest, where she allegedly assaulted two flight attendants onboard a Delta Los Angeles-New York flight. “Hi. It’s me, and I know I’ve been quiet for a couple of weeks since October 11th, and you deserve to hear from me directly, and I’m sorry that it’s taken this long,” the actress said in an Instagram video Friday. “There is a legal matter going on, and my lawyers have asked me to not say anything about that day, and I’m listening to them. And I take this very seriously.” The Legally Blonde star noted that “what I can tell you though is very simple, and the truest thing I know about myself [is] that not one day ever have I intended to hurt or frighten anyone, a day in my life.” She continued, “And so to the people that I disappointed, that I hurt, that I frightened, alarmed; I am so sorry.” Related Stories General News Selma Blair Speaks Out on Plane Arrest: "Did Not Intend to Harm Anyone" General News Selma Blair Is Accused of Assaulting Four People. Can Her Career Survive Another Scandal? Blair was arrested at John F. Kennedy International Airport on Oct. 11 after an alleged incident on a Delta plane that resulted in two flight attendants being injured and one being sent to the hospital. Blair was also transported to the hospital after the outburst, and she also allegedly repeatedly kicked the police officer who took her to the hospital and a nurse in the chest. She pleaded not guilty to two counts of assault, while separate charges from the FBI are expected to come as the agency investigates all assaults that occur onboard aircrafts. Blair thanked those who have reached out and “sent wishes of love or caring. It has meant everything to me and my son, who is my world, as a scout who is also OK.” “So right now, I’m going to be taking care of my health and my son and thinking of you all with gratitude and love,” she concluded. Blair’s spokesperson previously spoke out , releasing a statement that read, “Selma Blair experienced a medical emergency on the flight. There was no attempt to open the door of the aircraft. Selma did not intend to harm anyone.” Her attorney Shawn Barnes said in a court appearance after the incident that Blair had been working “extensive hours and exhaustive hours” ahead of the flight, and also hit her head on a bankhead. “These factors, coupled with the altitude, resulted in a state of severe confusion and disorientation,” Barnes said in court. In a separate statement, Blair’s rep said, “The suggestion by anyone that Selma does not have multiple sclerosis is outrageous,” she has the neurological condition pseudobulbar affect, “which bears directly on how a medical episode presents to people who do not know her.” “It should be noted Selma has worked on seven film and television projects in 2026 alone, only a couple of which have been announced. She has launched a skin care line, a clothing line, and a line of eye-glass readers, each built around the idea of beauty and utility for people whose bodies do not always cooperate,” the rep continued. “She remains a visible and relentless advocate for disability rights, for the MS community, and this year for the Jewish community in the face of rising antisemitism, including from the stage of the ADL’s State of the Arts event at The Jewish Museum two weeks ago. Selma had never been arrested before Sunday night. There is much more to this story than has been reported, and we ask to consider the entirety of the facts before rushing to judgment, whether in the courtroom or in the court of public opinion.” THR
